newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela inaugurates lower cost oil development.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inaugurates lower cost oil development.

text.p: Corpoven, a subsidiary of state- owned Petroleos de Venezuela, plans to increase oil production from the Bosque-Bucare fields from 27,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 140,000 bpd by 2000 through a partnership with Intevep, another PDVSA subsidiary, Corpoven said in a statement on Monday.
The five-year deal is intended to cut field development time by 45 percent, halve capital costs and ease technology transfer.
Corpoven said the Intevep partnership marked the beginning of a new cost-cutting plan, called ECO, with roots in the North Sea CRINE (Cost Reduction Initiative for the New Era) program.

"Maximum production had been forecast for 2006, but thanks to the partnership between Intevep and Corpoven and the application of the ECO plan, peak production is expected in 2000," the statement said.
Located in northeastern Venezuela, the Bosque-Bucare fields contain a light 34 degree API crude, but also involve a complex geological structure and a sensitive environment.
